title: If I had known, I wish
goal: Talk about past regrets with if + had, and use “I wish” correctly
intro: To imagine a different past, use if + had + past participle, then would have + past participle: “If I had known, I would have come.” “I wish” works the same way: wish + past for now (“I wish I had a car”), and wish + had done for the past (“I wish I had studied more”).

rules.rule: Different past: if + had done, would have done.
examples: If I had left earlier, I wouldn’t have missed the bus.
If you had asked, I would have helped.

rules.rule: I wish + past = I want the present to be different.
examples: I wish I lived near the sea.
I wish I could speak French.

rules.rule: I wish + had done = a regret about the past.
examples: I wish I had listened to you.
She wishes she hadn’t said that.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have known, I would have come.
mistakes.right: If I had known, I would have come.

mistakes.wrong: If you told me, I would have come.
mistakes.right: If you had told me, I would have come.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I have a car.
mistakes.right: I wish I had a car.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I studied harder in school.
mistakes.right: I wish I had studied harder in school.

ex.q: If I ___ about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
If she had studied, she ___ passed.
I wish I ___ that email. It was a mistake.
If I would have seen you, I would have said hi.
ex.fixed: If I had seen you, I would have said hi.

ex.q: If we had taken a taxi, we would reach on time.
ex.fixed: If we had taken a taxi, we would have reached on time.

ex.q: I wish I ___ (not / eat) so much. I feel sick.

ex.a: If you had called me, I would have helped.
ex.y: if + had done, would have done

ex.q: Say a regret with “I wish”: you didn’t learn music as a child.
a: I wish I had learned music*
I wish I had learnt music*
ex.y: I wish I had learned music as a child.

talk: Talk about one thing you wish were different in your life now, and one decision from the past: what would have happened if you had chosen differently?
